scenarios.title: Choose independent WAN paths for a branch
scenarios.summary: Keep a branch workstation connected to an application at another site during either supplied carrier outage.
scenarios.objective: Use at most two optional connections while keeping all fixed links attached. Give the branch desk a path to the dispatch application in ordinary operation and during either supplied carrier outage. Preserve a reply path during the Ferry outage. Keep the visitor device separate from the dispatch application.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Trace the failed trial, read what is unavailable, then inspect the supplied connection endpoints.

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: A wide area network (WAN) connects separate sites. Each site edge connects its local network to a carrier. A circuit is a connection offered between endpoints.

guide.title: Try the separate example
guide.why: Two circuits can use the same carrier. Both can work normally but fail together if the shared carrier is unavailable. Read which circuit options the supplied outage removes.

guide.title: Complete the independent assignment
guide.why: Compare both carrier outages and check a reply path as well. Connecting an unrelated visitor link can also open an unintended path. Keep all required separation while staying within the connection budget.

scenarios.explanation: The dual-carrier layout meets the stated outage trials. Both directions use available fixed and selected links, and the visitor remains separate.
hints: Look at the Condition row for each outage before changing connections.
The two Ferry options share the same stated outage. Inspect the fixed and optional endpoints to find an independent path.
Check the visitor before handing over the plan. An otherwise working branch path can still violate separation.
scenarios.simplifications: The path trace uses supplied ready-to-forward structural links and the stated outages. There is no real carrier, cloud deployment, IP forwarding or convergence, traffic timing, actual equipment, external service, or physical diversity certification.

scenarios.title: Keep local and hosted office services reachable
scenarios.summary: Keep printing within a small office and verify a hosted order desk through either supplied carrier outage.
scenarios.objective: Use at most three optional connections and keep the printer reachable in ordinary operation and without the fixed office uplink. Give the laptop a path to the hosted order desk in ordinary operation and during both supplied carrier outages. Keep the visitor kiosk separate from the printer and the hosted order desk.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Trace the failed trial, read what is unavailable, then inspect the supplied connection endpoints.

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: A small office/home office (SOHO) may keep its printer on the local network. A print job in this exercise travels from the studio laptop to the office gateway and then the printer.

guide.title: Try the separate example
guide.why: A hosted service is supplied at another site. Its path needs an office uplink, carrier and hosted edge. An uplink outage can prevent access to the hosted service while local printing continues.

guide.title: Complete the independent assignment
guide.why: Check printing with an office uplink down. Compare each carrier outage for the hosted service. Keep the visitor off the paths to both destinations.

scenarios.explanation: The printer stays reachable inside the office while the hosted service uses the surviving carrier. The visitor has no path to either service.
hints: Find the printer’s endpoint before selecting another uplink. Its connection stays in the office.
Trace the hosted service during each provider outage, and inspect the fixed links at the hosted edge.
Keep the visitor disconnected from paths to both authorized destinations.
scenarios.simplifications: The path trace uses supplied ready-to-forward structural links and the stated outages. There is no real carrier, cloud deployment, IP forwarding or convergence, traffic timing, actual equipment, external service, or physical diversity certification.
